body.statement: There is an algorithm which, from \(\mathfrak G\in\mathfrak E\) and \(m\in\mathbb N\), outputs a finite rational class \(\mathfrak F_{\mathfrak G,m}\), one common core radius, a common recession fan refining every nonempty component \(P_{v,b}\) with all incidence maps and semantic projections, rational chart meshes, rational partitions of unity, and a computable number \(\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(m)\downarrow0\) such that for every \(K\in\mathcal C_{\eta}\) there exists \(\widetilde K_m\in\mathfrak F_{\mathfrak G,m}\) whose semantic-label coverage is at least \(1-\eta-\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(m)\), whose separated risk is at most \(R_r(K)+D\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(m)\), and whose complete weighted ledger satisfies \(\rho_{\mathrm{led}}\le\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(m)\).
body.justification: This unchanged theorem is the global kernel required to turn coherent recession operators into one finite, auditable, globally honest search space with an input-computable error modulus.
body.gap: The unresolved step is not commutativity. It is simultaneous canonical-section safety for every active label and \(H_r\), safety of every positive-weight collar candidate, noncircular control of actual face--cone discrepancies, translated-uniform tails, and explicit refinement complexity \(N_j\) permitting schedules with \(N_j/L_j\to0\).
body.consumer: CertGluePFL termination and replayable global Gaussian certificates consume ECD only conditionally; no unconditional certificate consequence is asserted while this node remains to-prove.

obligation.what_is_open: Construct, or refute by a specific encoded experiment, one finite shared-trace recession library with an input-computable refinement schedule whose incident face--cone Gaussian-weighted discrepancies vanish while semantic coverage and separated risk are preserved uniformly over translated means. A valid construction must prove canonical-section preservation for every active label and for \(H_r\); safety of every candidate assigned positive collar weight; an exact overlap identity or an honest bound for the actual face--cone discrepancies; translated-uniform guard and normal-base tail bounds; and an explicit refinement count \(N_j\) with computable schedules \(L_j,B_j,\delta_j\) satisfying \(N_j/L_j\to0\).
obligation.obstruction: Finite rational active-set analysis currently proves only forward distance monotonicity from a fixed mean; it does not prove that a canonical normal section preserves each active semantic label or membership in \(H_r\) throughout every protected star. Fubini's theorem controls one affine section but not every piecewise collar candidate that receives positive weight. Equality of shared finite-element vertices holds on the geometric face, not throughout simultaneous face and cone collar supports. Defining a face trace by restricting the already-glued global rule would make the compatibility argument circular, while constant extension of a lower-skeleton rule can activate an unsafe candidate. Finally, the number \(N_j\) of refined cells is not bounded, so the sum of cellwise weighted discrepancies cannot be absorbed into an input-only constant and no verified choice currently yields \(N_j/L_j\to0\).
obligation.attempted: The shared-trace attempt began with one Gaussian-smoothed ancestor, placed all cones on a common rational simplicial refinement, used literally shared one-dimensional common-ray averaging factors, and proposed an induction over the barycentric recession skeleton with long angular and radial collars. Common-ray commutativity proves the operator cocycle, path independence, and translation boundary ratios. Global shared mesh vertices prove equality only on their common geometric faces. Protected-neighborhood charges and full-set repair account for certified failures once localized, but the required localization and simultaneous semantic and risk safety were not proved. Classical invariant-mean and Foelner results for one amenable commuting action do not supply these effective branching-poset estimates, so no further generic averaging reroll is asserted.
obligation.partial_result:
Starting from the single ancestor \(q_s=K*\phi_{s^2\Sigma}\), the established common-ray construction proves, for every face inclusion \(\tau\preceq\sigma\),
\[
q_{\sigma,L}
=
\left(
\prod_{\varrho\in\mathscr R(\sigma)\setminus\mathscr R(\tau)}
\mathsf A_{\varrho,L}
\right)q_{\tau,L},
\]
independently of the incidence path.  For every \(a\geq0\) and every shared ray \(\varrho\in\mathscr R(\sigma)\), it also proves
\[
\left\|q_{\sigma,L}(w+a\varrho)-q_{\sigma,L}(w)\right\|_1
\leq 2\min\{1,a/L\},
\]
and, for every \(f:\mathcal A\to[0,R_f]\),
\[
\left|F^f_{\sigma,L}(w+a\varrho)-F^f_{\sigma,L}(w)\right|
\leq R_f\min\{1,a/L\}.
\]
Together with Gaussian smoothing, single-chart averaging, and weighted path telescoping, every fixed finite library therefore has the computable error terms
\[
R_f\min\{1,s^2\sqrt{d/8}\},
\qquad
\frac{R_fk}{T\sqrt{2\pi}},
\qquad
\sum_e\Gamma_{C,e}^f+\frac{R_f}{2}\omega(h).
\]
These facts do not imply that the Gaussian-weighted difference between an incident cone rule and its face rule vanishes.  Nor do they establish simultaneous semantic coverage on every \(D_v\) and separated-risk preservation on \(H_r\), uniformly over translated means.  Closing the target additionally requires canonical-section preservation for every active label and for \(H_r\), safety of every candidate receiving positive collar weight, an exact overlap identity or a quantitative bound for the actual face--cone discrepancy, translated-uniform guard and normal-base tail bounds, and an explicit refinement count \(N_j\) with computable schedules \(L_j,B_j,\delta_j\) satisfying \(N_j/L_j\to0\).
